summary: Panama’s restoration pledge is 100,000 ha of ecosystems in 2026–2035, including 2,500 ha of degraded mangrove, alongside a net-zero-deforestation goal; this equals about 2.1% of current forest cover. A 50,000 ha forest-restoration pledge by 2050 equals 1.0% of forest. A support-dependent 130,000 ha of degraded land will be restored through agroforestry and silvopastoral systems by 2050—about 5.6% of current agriculture—with 15% completed by 2030. Measures cover 1,800 ha of mangroves by 2028 and 1,000 ha of coastal wetlands by 2030. Conservation commitments include protecting 40% of terrestrial territory and 60% of seas by 2035, maintaining 68% forest cover, integrating at least 50% of mangroves into the national protected-area system by 2026, and establishing three biological corridors while reducing unplanned agricultural expansion by 30%. Panama seeks a 10 million km² high-seas protected area, 600 ha of silvopastoral farming, and pilots in three priority watersheds; some measures are support-dependent.
